checks_run.actual: (a) Exit 0: 20 files, 198 tests passed, 0 skipped. Sweep: 560 requests per reader over 374 operations (525 ids), 73 operations not fillable (named in the log), and 367 read with 2xx by an admitted reader. Disclosed: while this ran, the kernel OOM-killed a process in my session's shared memory limit. Vitest reported no failure or worker loss, and the root e2e that was running at the same time was later affected (DOM-R7-07). (b) D-218 is met as designed. References are omitted or nulled with includesRestrictedRecords and a typed marker (countedBenefitRestricted, evidenceRestricted and so on), so a counted member or an existing override never reads as 'none'. Re-saves keep hidden links (group PATCH, Day-90 answer, custom values, agenda), which protects evidence integrity against a not-admitted editor. A gate submission shown to a not-admitted reader is redacted while the stored snapshot and snapshotSha256 stay intact. The contract says the redacted view does not verify against the hash, and the record carries the label, so the approval stays tied to its unchanged evidence snapshot. D-219, which I accept: the audit trail does give a not-admitted TL or AUD the opaque id of a sensitive record's own events. That id carries no content (changes and reason are null), GET on it answers 404 exactly as for a missing record, and the record's existence is already conveyed by the 'Includes restricted records' label. Nulling it would break a complete, tamper-evident trail. The grant register is shown only to sensitive_record.read holders, who administer grants by record id. The phase-step remove echo returns an id the writer itself sent. I could not show a disclosure through these paths that gives the reader anything beyond the existence the product already discloses. (c) BE-Z7B residuals, all acceptable under ADR-0051: the 73 (was 75) unfillable GETs, because the sweep guards the shared rule and is not the control; search, which is covered after a real indexing run by A12 (26/26 in DOM-R7-08); the flag-only adoption filter, because no adoption item is a sensitive type and ADR-0051 §2 binds the change that would make one restrictable; and the omitted-table totals, which FE-Z3 has now fixed (DOM-R7-06). (d) concurrent-exception-recurrence 7/7 and exception-recurrence-race 7/7 (p6-integration.log). Their source is unchanged since round 6, where my mutant failed all 7 F-DG6-380 tests. I keep my round-6 judgement: under the advisory lock and FOR UPDATE, greatest(now(), column) reads the latest committed row, and occurrence_count steps by exactly 1 under the version guard, so no occurrence is lost or counted twice, which is the 0101 guard's intent.
